source.title: BUB1B promotes homologous recombination-mediated DNA damage repair in breast cancer cells through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
source.reading_scope: Targeted primary-source reading of relevant model, shRNA, radiation assay, Results and figure-caption sections; no raw data reanalysis or full-paper independent reproduction.

experiment.intervention: Stable shRNA BUB1B knockdown versus non-targeting control
experiment.radiation: 8 Gy ionizing radiation; reported dose rate 1 Gy/min for gamma-H2AX immunofluorescence; neutral comet assay at 2 hours after 8 Gy

xenograft.intervention: Unirradiated xenograft from control or shBUB1B MDA-MB-231 cells
xenograft.result: Tumor growth lower in the BUB1B-knockdown group

without_radiation: BUB1B knockdown reduced proliferation/colony formation and EdU incorporation
after_radiation: BUB1B knockdown increased neutral-comet tail moment

competitive_implication.classification: Tumor-compatibility context, not a drug efficacy candidate
competitive_implication.inference: A BUBR1-restoring intervention could alter tumor DNA-damage responses if it changes tumor-cell BUBR1; this paper does not establish that restoration promotes radioresistance or worsens cancer outcomes.
competitive_implication.design_consequence: If radiation is part of the confirmed oncology regimen, test the actual candidate with and without that regimen in a relevant tumor model, separately from nonmalignant muscle function.
